prime_award_base_transaction_description: PROJECT TITLE:  MINING IMPACTS AND RESTORATION POTENTIAL FOR JUVENILE CHINOOK SALMON IN COAL CREEK (YUKON CHARLEY NATIONAL PRESERVE, ALASKA).PROJECT PERIOD: 08 01 2026 - 06 30 2027THIS PROJECT DESCRIBES DATA SYNTHESIS AND ANALYSIS TO BE DONE FOLLOWING RESEARCH AND MONITORING AT COAL CREEK (YUKON-CHARLEY RIVERS NATIONAL PRESERVE, ALASKA). IT IS INTENDED TO SPAN A ONE-YEAR PERIOD. THE RESEARCH CENTERS ON TWO THEMES: 1) FISH ORIGINS AND HABITAT USE AND 2) AQUATIC HABITAT ASSESSMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION, BOTH IN SUPPORT OF THE RESTORATION AND BROADER ACTIVITIES TO SUPPORT PACIFIC SALMON POPULATION RECOVERY THROUGHOUT THE YUKON RIVER BASIN. SEEKING TO BETTER QUANTIFY PRESENT AND POTENTIAL (RESTORED STREAM) FUTURE USE OF COAL CREEK BY CHINOOK AND OTHER PACIFIC SALMON SPECIES, IN ADDITION TO OTHER FISHES. THE BULK OF EFFORTS WILL BE TO CHARACTERIZE THE ENERGETIC REQUIREMENTS AND POTENTIAL FOR SALMON GROWTH IN COAL CREEK, BASED ON TEMPERATURE AND FOOD WEB SAMPLING. A MAJOR INTENDED OUTCOME OF THIS RESEARCH OVERALL IS TO HELP MEET THE INTERESTS OF THE NATIONAL PARK SERVICE AND RESTORATION PRACTITIONERS IN UNDERSTANDING WHAT BENEFITS COAL CREEK IS CURRENTLY PROVIDING TO SALMON AND OTHER FISHES, PARTICULARLY CHINOOK SALMON. IT ALSO SEEKS, CRITICALLY, TO PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS AND PREDICTIONS ABOUT HOW MINING AND RESTORATION ACTIVITIES MAY IMPACT THESE CONDITIONS, BOTH LOCALLY WITHIN COAL CREEK AND BASIN-WIDE. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED - THIS IS A DATA SYNTHESIS PROJECT  ALL SAMPLES WERE COLLECTED AND PROCESSED PREVIOUSLY. COLLECTIVELY, DATA WILL BE USED IN A MULTI-PARAMETER FRAMEWORK BASED ON GENERALIZED LINEAR MODELS AND NON-METRIC MULTIDIMENSIONAL SCALING ORDINATIONS TO COMPARE AND CONTRAST FOOD AND HABITAT CONDITIONS IN COAL CREEK AGAINST LESS-IMPACTED REFERENCE SITES. LEVERAGING FISH BIOENERGETICS MODELS TAILORED TO SUBARCTIC CHINOOK SALMON POPULATIONS, WILL EXPLORE THE EXTENT TO WHICH COAL CREEK MAY SUPPORT JUVENILE CHINOOK SALMON GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT, AND HOW THIS GROWTH POTENTIAL MAY BE IMPROVED BY LOCALIZED RESTORATION. BECAUSE INSTREAM MINING IS COMMON AND EXTENSIVE THROUGHOUT THE YUKON RIVER WATERSHED, RESEARCH WILL BE CONCLUDED BY USING COAL CREEK AS A CASE STUDY FOR HOW MINING IMPACTS AND RESTORATION MAY INTERACT TO INFLUENCE CHINOOK SALMON POPULATION HEALTH ACROSS THE YUKON RIVER BASIN. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES -THIS PROJECT WILL SUPPORT THE FIRST YEAR OF A PROGRAM FOR A MASTERS STUDENT IN FISHERIES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF), WITH COAL CREEK RESEARCH FORMING THE ENTIRETY OF THEIR THESIS RESEARCH. THIS ACADEMIC PRODUCT AND SUBSEQUENT SCIENTIFIC JOURNAL PUBLICATIONS AND SCIENTIFIC MEETING PRESENTATIONS WILL BE THE MAJOR INTELLECTUAL PRODUCTS EMANATING FROM THIS RESEARCH. FOR NPS AND OTHER INTERESTED PARTNERS, REPORTS WILL BE DEVELOPED AS NEEDED TO BEST SUIT THE NEEDS OF THE PROJECT. AT LEAST TWO SCIENTIFIC PAPERS TO BE PUBLISHED IN SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS ARE ALSO EXPECTED AS OUTCOMES OF THIS RESEARCH, ALONG WITH AT LEAST TWO PRESENTATIONS AT SCIENTIFIC CONFERENCES. INTENDED BENEFICIARY(IES) -THE PRINCIPAL BENEFICIARY OF THE RESEARCH CARRIED OUT UNDER THIS AWARD WILL BE THE NATIONAL PARK SERVICE AND ITS RESEARCH AND MANGEMENT STAFF, WHO ARE PRESENTLY PLANNING AND IMPLEMENTING RESTORATION ACTIVITIES AT COAL CREEK. ADDITIONAL BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE COMMUNITIES, PARTICULARLY INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES IN THE VICINITY OF COAL CREEK ALONG THE YUKON RIVER, WHO RELY ON SALMON FOR THEIR LIVELIHOODS. REGIONAL LAND MANAGERS WITH THE ALASKA DEPARTMENT OF FISH AND GAME, US BUREAU OF LAND MANAGEMENT, AND US FISH AND WILDLIFE SERVICE WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THIS RESEARCH IN UNDERSTANDING CHANGES TO THE LANDS, WATERS, AND FISHERIES THEY MANAGE. SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES, IF KNOWN OR SPECIFIED AT THE TIME OF AWARD -NONE KNOWN.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: EPIDEMIOLOGIC MODELING TO IDENTIFY OPTIMAL EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE HIV INCIDENCE IN ALABAMA - PROJECT SUMMARY ALABAMA (AL), A PRIORITY STATE IN THE U.S. ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC INITIATIVE, REQUIRES SUBSTANTIAL PUBLIC HEALTH RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY OPTIMAL HIV INTERVENTION STRATEGIES IN SUPPORT OF GREATER HIV CONTROL. AMONG PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV IN AL, ONLY 61% HAVE ACHIEVED VIRAL SUPPRESSION IN COMPARISON TO 65% FOR THE U.S. AVERAGE RATE AND FAR FROM THE 2030 NATIONAL GOALS OF 90%. BETTER HIV CONTROL IN AL CAN BE ACHIEVED BY LEVERAGING PUBLIC HEALTH DATA TO IDENTIFY AND PRIORITY RANK EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS (EBIS) THAT ARE MOST EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT. PARTICULARLY, MATHEMATICAL MODELING CAN BE USED TO GENERATE THE EVIDENCE. CURRENTLY, THE K01 CANDIDATE WORKS WITH UNIVERSITY OF ALABAMA AT BIRMINGHAM (UAB) INVESTIGATORS TO IMPLEMENT A NIAID-FUNDED R01 EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL EVALUATING THREE COMBINATION EBIS IN THE SOUTHWESTERN REGION OF THE STATE. WHILE THIS TRIAL WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO CLINICAL AND IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES, IT DOES NOT CURRENTLY INCLUDE PLANS TO ESTIMATE THE POTENTIAL REDUCTION IN HIV INCIDENCE OR IMPACT OF AN EXPANDED SET OF EBIS. THUS, THE K01 CANDIDATE HAS AN UNMATCHED OPPORTUNITY TO EMBED MATHEMATICAL MODELING WITHIN THIS R01 TRIAL AND BEYOND, AND ENGAGE WITH PUBLIC HEALTH AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS IN A PARTICIPATORY HIV EPIDEMIOLOGIC MODELING APPROACH THAT WILL YIELD PUBLIC HEALTH DATA THAT CAN GUIDE STATE HIV INTERVENTION PLANNING WHILE ADVANCING HER CAREER. SPECIFIC AIMS ARE: (1) TO USE MATHEMATICAL MODELING TO DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL FOUR-YEAR IMPACT OF THREE EBIS TO REDUCE HIV INCIDENCE (EPIDEMIOLOGIC BENEFITS) IN THE COASTAL REGION OF AL. GUIDED BY FEEDBACK FROM PUBLIC HEALTH LEADERS AND THE R01 TRIAL DATA, WE WILL BUILD A COMPARTMENTAL MODEL TO SIMULATE THE HIV EPIDEMIC IN THE COASTAL AL REGION AND EVALUATE THE THREE EBIS’ IMPACT. AIM 2: TO ASSESS THE IMPACT OF A) STATEWIDE SCALE-UP OF THE THREE STUDIED EBIS AND B) EXPANDED COVERAGE TO ADDITIONAL EBIS RECOMMENDED BY THE CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION (CDC). GUIDED BY KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS WITH PUBLIC HEALTH LEADERS, WE WILL EXPAND AIM 1 MODEL TO SIMULATE THE STATEWIDE HIV EPIDEMIC AND EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF SELECTED EBIS FROM THE CDC COMPENDIUM IN REDUCING HIV INCIDENCE. AIM 3: TO USE PARTICIPATORY HIV MODELING FOR THE SELECTION OF OPTIMAL HIV INTERVENTION STRATEGIES FOR AL. WE WILL CONDUCT KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS WITH PUBLIC HEALTH LEADERS USING MODELING FINDINGS FROM AIMS 1 AND 2. THROUGH DISCUSSIONS WE WILL INFORM PUBLIC HEALTH LEADERS AND FACILITATE CONSENSUS WHICH WILL BE FOLLOWED BY ITERATIVELY CUSTOMIZING ANALYSES, YIELDING PRIORITY RANKING OF THE EBIS FOR AL. BY ADDRESSING THE K01 AIMS, DR. NGHIEM WILL GAIN IN-DEPTH TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE IN PARTICIPATORY HIV EPIDEMIOLOGIC MODELING, INCLUDING MATHEMATICAL MODELING, QUALITATIVE RESEARCH, AND DISSEMINATION SCIENCE, POSITIONING HER TO BECOME AN INDEPENDENTLY FUNDED RESEARCHER.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: ARCH REACH: ARCH CENTER FOR RESEARCH AT THE INTERSECTION OF EQUITY, ALCOHOL, COMMUNITY AND HIV - ABSTRACT THE ALCOHOL RESEARCH CONSORTIUM IN HIV CENTER FOR RESEARCH AT THE INTERSECTION OF EQUITY, ALCOHOL, COMMUNITY AND HIV (ARCH REACH) SEEKS TO OPTIMIZE WELL-BEING AMONG PWH AND ACCELERATE PROGRESS TOWARDS ENDING THE HIV EPIDEMIC (EHE) BY ADDRESSING CO-OCCURRING UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE (UAU). GROUNDED IN HEALTH EQUITY AND WITH CAREFUL ATTENTION TO SOCIAL AND STRUCTURAL DRIVERS OF HEALTH, WE WILL EXPAND THE SCOPE AND RELEVANCE OF SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE AND TREATMENT INTERVENTIONS AT THE INTERSECTION OF THE HIV CARE CONTINUUM, THE ALCOHOL CARE CONTINUUM, AND HIV-RELATED COMORBIDITIES. WE WILL DO THIS BY DEVELOPING, TAILORING, AND IMPLEMENTING EVIDENCE- BASED INTERVENTIONS (EBIS) FOR ALCOHOL REDUCTION THAT ARE ACCESSIBLE TO PWH WITH UAU; ADDRESSING SYNDEMIC CONDITIONS IN OUR INTERVENTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND EPIDEMIOLOGY WORK; ACTIVELY ENGAGING PWH WITH DIVERSE LIVED EXPERIENCES IN OUR CENTER; AND EXPANDING THE DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION OF PROJECT RESEARCHERS AND TRAINEES. OUR SCIENTIFIC GOALS ARE TO: 1) INCREASE THE REACH OF ALCOHOL EBIS THROUGH IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL RESEARCH AT THE INTERSECTION OF UAU AND HIV, 2) EXPAND OUR HIV RESEARCH TO INCORPORATE NEW DEFINITIONS OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER RECOVERY, AND 3) INCREASE INCLUSIVITY/DIVERSITY OF PERSPECTIVES IN ARCH REACH THROUGH COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT AND MENTORING OF TRAINEES. WE PROPOSE A HIGHLY INTERACTIVE AND SYNERGISTIC CENTER WITH THREE PROJECTS SUPPORTED BY ADMINISTRATIVE, METHODS, AND DISSEMINATION CORES. ARCH REACH IS EMBEDDED IN AND CAPITALIZES ON THE RESEARCH AND CLINICAL INFRASTRUCTURE OF THE CENTER FOR AIDS RESEARCH NETWORK OF INTEGRATED CLINICAL SYSTEMS (CNICS), A MULTI-SITE CLINICAL COHORT REPRESENTING TEN UNIVERSITY-BASED HIV CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES (US)—WITH MANY LOCATED IN HIGH PRIORITY REGIONS FOR EHE. THE FIRST PROJECT LEVERAGES CNICS DATA TO EXAMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN UAU, UAU TREATMENTS, AND NEW DEFINITIONS OF AUD RECOVERY ON HIV TREATMENT OUTCOMES AND COMORBIDITIES AMONG PWH IN THE CONTEXT OF SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH. OUR SECOND PROJECT, USING HUMAN CENTERED DESIGN METHODS, WILL ADAPT, TAILOR, AND PILOT TEST AN ALCOHOL EBI FOR TELEPHONE DELIVERY IN A HYBRID TYPE 1 EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION STUDY. LASTLY, OUR THIRD PROJECT, A HYBRID TYPE 2 EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN, WILL TAILOR AND IMPLEMENT A SYNDEMIC CONDITIONS INTERVENTION FOR UAU AND CO-OCCURRING MENTAL HEALTH DISORDERS USING AN AUDIT AND FEEDBACK IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY. AN ADMINISTRATIVE CORE WILL PROVIDE THE STRUCTURE AND PROCESSES TO SUPPORT COLLABORATION AND SYNERGY ACROSS ARCH REACH PROJECTS AND INVESTIGATORS. A METHODS CORE WILL SUPPORT IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE AIMS OF PROJECTS AND DEVELOP NOVEL ANALYTIC METHODS. LASTLY, A DISSEMINATION CORE WILL ASSEMBLE A TRANSDISCIPLINARY COMMUNITY PARTNER BOARD AND SUPPORT THE DISSEMINATION OF PROJECT FINDINGS TO ENSURE THE EQUITABLE UPTAKE, RECEIPT, AND DELIVERY OF EBIS FOR UAU. CAPITALIZING ON A STRONG ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, THE EXTENSIVE RESOURCES AND INFRASTRUCTURE OF CNICS, AND A TRANSDISCIPLINARY TEAM INCLUSIVE OF COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ARCH REACH ADDRESSES ISSUES OF HIGH RELEVANCE TO US EHE GOALS BY ADDRESSING THE INTERSECTION OF HIV, ALCOHOL USE, AND HEALTH EQUITY.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: GENETIC AND SINGLE-CELL MULTI-OMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE RISK AND RESILIENCE PATHWAYS - PROJECT SUMMARY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A DEVASTATING AND COMPLEX NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER WITH A CRUSHING SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC BURDEN CURRENTLY AFFECTING MORE THAN 6 MILLION PATIENTS IN THE US. WITH THE NUMBER OF AFFECTED INDIVIDU- ALS PROJECTED TO INCREASE, IDENTIFYING DISEASE-MODIFYING TREATMENTS AND INTERVENTIONS FOR AD REMAINS ONE OF THE MOST CRITICAL UNDERTAKINGS IN MODERN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH. A CRITICAL STEP TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE INTERVEN- TIONS INVOLVES CHARACTERIZING THE GENES AND PATHWAYS MEDIATING AD RISK AND RESILIENCE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO EXPLORE THE MODULATION OF AD GENETIC RISK BY AGE AND EXAMINE HOW CALORIC RESTRICTION (CR), A LIFESPAN-INCREASING INTERVENTION, CAN BE HARNESSED TO COUNTER AD RISK. THE PROPOSAL WILL UTILIZE STATE-OF- THE-ART SINGLE-NUCLEI MULTI-OMIC FUNCTIONAL GENOMIC ANALYSES OF HEALTHY AND AD HUMAN BRAIN TISSUE, AS WELL AS TRANSGENIC AD MOUSE MODELS, TO PERFORM DEEP MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION OF AD RISK AND RESILIENCE ACROSS THE GENETIC, EPIGENOMIC, AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC LAYERS. AIM 1 WILL DISSECT NON-CODING AD GENETIC RISK THROUGH INTENSIVE MULTI-OMIC MOLECULAR PROFILING OF HEALTHY AND AD BRAINS, ALLOWING THE NOMINATION OF CAUSAL VARIANTS, CELL TYPES, AND PATHWAYS MEDIATING RISK. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE MECHANISMS IN COGNITIVELY HEALTHY, LONG-LIVED INDIVID- UALS, INCLUDING CENTENARIANS, AND DETERMINE WHETHER AD RESILIENCE MANIFESTS BY MAINTAINING A “YOUNG” STATE OR BY COMPENSATING FOR DETRIMENTAL AGE-RELATED EFFECTS AND AD GENETIC RISK. THIS WILL INVOLVE COMPARISON ACROSS A BROAD AGE SPECTRUM, INCLUDING MOLECULAR PROFILES OF YOUNG CONTROLS (AGED 18-35) AND AD PATIENTS. AIM 3 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN CR AND NEURODEGENERATION IN GENETICALLY DIVERSE AD MOUSE MODELS. THIS WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO THE PATHWAYS MEDIATING LIFESPAN-INCREASING INTERVENTIONS IN THE BRAIN, THEIR INTERACTION WITH HIGH-RISK AND RESILIENT GENETIC BACKGROUNDS, AND THEIR OVERLAP WITH AD RISK AND RESILIENCE PATHWAYS IN HU- MANS. IMPORTANTLY, THIS PROPOSAL WILL DIRECTLY ADDRESS THE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN LIFESPAN AND AD RESILIENCE TO PROVIDE A MORE NUANCED UNDERSTANDING OF THE POTENTIAL OF CR AND ITS MIMETICS AS THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR AD. THIS PROPOSAL EMPLOYS AN INNOVATIVE RESEARCH APPROACH COMBINING OBSERVATIONAL AND INTERVENTIONAL STUDY DE- SIGNS WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART COMPUTATIONAL TECHNIQUES. THIS APPROACH FACILITATES CONCURRENT HUMAN AND MOUSE DATA ANALYSIS, EXPEDITING THE DISCOVERY OF MOLECULAR PATHWAYS MEDIATING AD RISK AND RESILIENCE, WITH POTENTIAL IMPLICATIONS FOR DEVELOPING NOVEL AD PREVENTION STRATEGIES. UNDER THE MENTORSHIP OF DR. HARARI AND CO-MENTORS DR. GOATE, KACZOROWSKI, KARCH, AND LEE, I WILL FOLLOW A RIGOROUS TRAINING PROGRAM TO MEET THE AIMS OF THIS K99/R00 AWARD AND TRANSITION INTO INDEPENDENT RESEARCH LEADERSHIP IN THE DOMAIN OF AD AND AGING. THIS WILL INCLUDE A FOCUS ON NEUROBIOLOGY, THE BIOLOGY OF AGING, MOUSE MODELS OF AD, BIOINFORMATICS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, ACHIEVED THROUGH COURSES, WORKSHOPS, CONFERENCES, AND ADVISORY COMMITTEE FEEDBACK. IN SUMMARY, THIS PRO- POSAL ADDRESSES A CRITICAL GAP IN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF AD AND AGING, WITH THE ADDITIONAL SKILLS ACQUIRED DURING THIS AWARD LAYING A SOLID FOUNDATION FOR MY FUTURE INDEPENDENCE IN THE MOLECULAR BIOLOGY OF AD.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: CG DINUCLEOTIDE-MEDIATED IMMUNE RESPONSES DURING WEST NILE VIRUS INFECTION - ABSTRACT VIRUSES CONTAIN GENETIC MATERIAL IN DNA OR RNA COMPOSED OF NUCLEOTIDES. FOR RNA, THESE NUCLEOTIDES ARE A (ADENINE), C (CYTOSINE), G (GUANINE), AND U (URACIL). TWO NUCLEOTIDES LINKED BY A PHOSPHATE MOLECULE, SUCH AS UA OR CG, ARE CALLED DINUCLEOTIDES. MANY RNA VIRUSES, INCLUDING FLAVIVIRUSES, HAVE EVOLVED TO MIMIC THE LOW CYTOSINE-PHOSPHATE-GUANINE (CG) DINUCLEOTIDE CONTENT OF VERTEBRATE GENOMES TO EVADE RECOGNITION BY HOST ZINC FINGER ANTIVIRAL PROTEIN 1 (ZAP), WHICH BINDS CG-RICH OR CG-ENRICHED NON-SELF RNA AND TARGETS IT FOR DEGRADATION. MANY VIRUSES HAVE ALSO EVOLVED REDUCED URACIL-PHOSPHATE-ADENINE (UA) DINUCLEOTIDE CONTENT TO EVADE RNA- DEGRADING ENZYMES AND POSSIBLY ZAP. ENRICHMENT OF CG AND UA DINUCLEOTIDES IN VIRAL RNA IS AN EMERGING PROMISING VACCINE APPROACH. IN ADDITION TO VACCINES, DINUCLEOTIDE ENRICHMENT IS AN EMERGING APPROACH FOR ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES. A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP FOR THE FURTHER RATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF SAFE AND PROTECTIVE VACCINES AND EFFECTIVE ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES IS THE LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF INNATE CELLULAR IMMUNE RESPONSES TO VIRUSES CARRYING CG/UA-ENRICHED RNA. THUS, IN THIS PROJECT, WE WILL STUDY HOW PERIPHERAL AND LYMPHOID DENDRITIC CELLS (DCS) INTERACT WITH CG-, UA-, AND CG/UA-ENRICHED VIRUSES. UNDERSTANDING INTERACTIONS WITH DCS IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THEY ARE ESSENTIAL FOR INITIATING THE EARLY ACTIVATION OF INFLAMMATORY MONOCYTES AND ADAPTIVE T CELL RESPONSES. MOREOVER, MANY VIRUSES, SUCH AS FLAVIVIRUSES LIKE WEST NILE VIRUS (WNV), HAVE EVOLVED TO IMPAIR DC ACTIVATION AND DC-MEDIATED STIMULATION OF T CELL ANTIVIRAL RESPONSES. WE WILL LEVERAGE CHARACTERIZED CG-, UA-, AND CG/UA-ENRICHED WNV VARIANTS, AS WELL AS THE WNV–HUMAN PERIPHERAL DC–T CELL INTERACTION MODEL. WE WILL ALSO USE THE CONVENTIONAL AND ZAP KNOCKOUT C57BL/6J MOUSE MODELS TO STUDY INTERACTIONS WITH LYMPHOID DCS. UNLIKE MANY HUMAN VIRUSES, WNV IS VIRULENT IN CONVENTIONAL C57BL/6J MICE, WHICH FACILITATES IMMUNE RESPONSE STUDIES. CLASSICAL VIROLOGY AND FLOW CYTOMETRY ASSAYS, BULK RNA-SEQ, AND STATE-OF-THE-ART SINGLE-CELL RNA-SEQ WILL BE USED IN THE PROJECT. WE WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST INSIGHTS INTO HOW CG-, UA-, AND CG/UA DINUCLEOTIDE-ENRICHED VIRUSES INTERACT WITH ESSENTIAL DC POPULATIONS, AND WHETHER DINUCLEOTIDE ENRICHMENT CAN OVERCOME DC IMPAIRMENT AND T CELL DYSFUNCTION INDUCED BY WILD-TYPE VIRUS INFECTION. THIS PROJECT WILL ADVANCE THE RATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF ENRICHED VACCINES AND ONCOLYTIC VIRUSES THAT SELECTIVELY ACTIVATE DINUCLEOTIDE-SPECIFIC BENEFICIAL IMMUNE PATHWAYS.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: INVESTIGATING THE IMPACT OF MENOPAUSE AND MENOPAUSE HORMONE THERAPY ON IMMUNE DETERMINANTS OF HIV-1 SUSCEPTIBILTY IN CERVICAL MUCOSA - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT AGING WOMEN REPRESENT A GROWING DEMOGRAPHIC WITH INCREASING HIV-1 INFECTION PREVALENCE AND INCIDENCE. ESTROGEN DECLINE, THE HALLMARK OF MENOPAUSE, LEADS TO IMMUNOSENESCENCE AND “INFLAMMAGING”, WHICH IS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED VULNERABILITY TO INFECTIONS. ESTROGEN REPLACEMENT VIA MENOPAUSAL HORMONE THERAPY (MHT) PARTIALLY RESTORES BLOOD IMMUNE CELL HOMEOSTASIS BUT IS UNDERSTUDIED FOR ITS IMPACT ON AGE-RELATED IMMUNE DECLINE IN CERVICOVAGINAL MUCOSA, A PRIMARY SITE OF SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS (STIS) INCLUDING HIV-1. IT IS OF SIGNIFICANCE TO DISCOVER HOW MENOPAUSE AND MHT RESHAPE MUCOSAL IMMUNE COMPETENCE AND IMPACT STI SUSCEPTIBILITY TO BETTER INFORM PATIENT AND HEALTHCARE PROVIDER DECISION MAKING, AND HIV-1 PREVENTION EFFORTS IN AGING WOMEN. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE CERVICAL MUCOSAL IMMUNE ENVIRONMENT IS ALTERED BY MENOPAUSE IN WAYS THAT ARE RELEVANT TO HIV-1 SUSCEPTIBILITY, AND THAT MHT MODULATES INNATE AND ADAPTIVE IMMUNOLOGICAL DETERMINANTS. OUR RESEARCH STRATEGY INTEGRATES (A) OUR HIGHLY SENSITIVE EX VIVO CERVICAL EXPLANT TISSUE (CET) MODEL TO STUDY INFECTION WITH TRANSMITTED/FOUNDER HIV-1 STRAINS WITH (B) HIGH-PARAMETER SPECTRAL FLOW CYTOMETRY, AND (C) SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING (SCRNA-SEQ) TO ASSESS THE HORMONE-REGULATED IMMUNOBIOLOGY OF CERVICAL TISSUE OBTAINED FROM PRE-, PERI- AND MENOPAUSAL WOMEN -/+ MHT WHO UNDERGO MEDICALLY INDICATED HYSTERECTOMIES AT UAB CLINICS. IN AIM 1, 34-COLOR FLOW CYTOMETRIC ANALYSES, CONDUCTED IN FLOWJO (TRADITIONAL GATING) AND AS UNBIASED CLUSTERING USING FLOWSOM AND TSNE/UMAP IN R, WILL SHOW HOW AGING AND HORMONAL DECLINE RESHAPE THE PHENOTYPES OF CERVICAL T-CELLS AND MACROPHAGES. WE WILL ALSO DISCOVER IMMUNE STATES THAT ARE EITHER ENHANCED OR DIMINISHED WITH MHT. FINDINGS FROM AIM 2 ON EX VIVO HIV-1 INFECTION IN CERVICAL TISSUE FROM WOMEN ACROSS THE LIFESPAN WILL BE INTEGRATED WITH IMMUNE PHENOTYPING DATA TO IDENTIFY CELLULAR DETERMINANTS OF HIV-1 SUSCEPTIBILITY ASSOCIATED WITH MENOPAUSE AND MHT USE. THESE ANALYSES WILL REVEAL WHETHER ESTROGEN LOSS ENHANCES, AND MHT MITIGATES CERVICAL TISSUE VULNERABILITY TO HIV-1 INFECTION EX VIVO. AIM 3 WILL GENERATE THE FIRST MENOPAUSE/MHT FOCUSED SINGLE-CELL TRANSCRIPTOME ATLAS OF CERVICAL MUCOSAL IMMUNOBIOLOGY AND TEST FOR CORRELATES OF SCRNA-SEQ DATA WITH PHENOTYPIC AND EX VIVO HIV-1 INFECTION/REPLICATION DATA FROM AIMS 1 AND 2. HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING SCRNA-SEQ DATA WILL UNDERPIN FUTURE MECHANISTIC STUDIES ON CANDIDATE BIOMARKERS AND HORMONE-REGULATED PATHWAYS. STUDY IMPACT: NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO HOW AGING-RELATED ESTROGEN LOSS AND MHT IMPACT CERVICAL IMMUNE FUNCTION AND VULNERABILITY TO HIV-1 WILL GUIDE FUTURE WORK TOWARDS THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF INFORMING AGING WOMEN’S CLINICAL HEALTH DECISION-MAKING, AND STI/HIV PREVENTION EFFORTS.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: EXAMINING THE EFFECT OF HIGH-INTENSITY EXERCISE TO ATTENUATE COGNITIVE FUNCTION LIMITATIONS AND TRAIN EXERCISE HABITS IN OLDER PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (HEALTH-COG) - PROJECT ABSTRACT/SUMMARY. THE POPULATION OF PEOPLE WITH HIV (PWH) IS AGING, AND ARE AT HIGHER RISK FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) THAN SERONEGATIVE COUNTERPARTS. ALTHOUGH PHYSICAL ACTIVITY (PA) IS A PROMISING PROTECTIVE FACTOR TO MITIGATE ADRD RISK, FEW WELL-POWERED PA INTERVENTION STUDIES HAVE RIGOROUSLY TESTED COGNITIVE OUTCOMES AMONG OLDER PWH, A POPULATION WITH RATES OF MODERATE TO VIGOROUS PA WELL BELOW RECOMMENDED GUIDELINES. FURTHER, GIVEN THAT ADHERENCE TO HABITUAL PA DIMINISHES AFTER SUPERVISED INTERVENTIONS, IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS OF ADHERENCE (MOA) TO HABITUAL PA AMONG OLDER PWH IS GERMANE TO DEVELOP EFFECTIVE AND DURABLE INTERVENTIONS TO PROTECT COGNITIVE HEALTH. THE PROPOSED R01 WILL LEVERAGE THE HIGH-INTENSITY EXERCISE STUDY TO ATTENUATE LIMITATIONS AND TRAIN HABITS IN OLDER ADULTS WITH HIV (HEALTH), A TWO-SITE RCT (UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON [UW], UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO DENVER [UCD]) OF 100 OLDER PWH EXAMINING: 1) IF 4 MONTHS OF SUPERVISED HIGH-INTENSITY INTERVAL TRAINING (HIIT) MITIGATES PHYSICAL FUNCTION IMPAIRMENTS AND FATIGUE TO A GREATER EXTENT THAN CONTINUOUS MODERATE EXERCISE (CME); 2) THE EFFECTS OF A 3 MONTH TEXT-MESSAGING INTERVENTION ON PA ADHERENCE. IN CONTRAST TO CME, WHERE AEROBIC EXERCISE IS PERFORMED CONTINUOUSLY FOR A SPECIFIED DURATION, HIIT, WHICH USES REPEATED ALTERNATING BOUTS OF HIGH-INTENSITY AND LOWER INTENSITY AEROBIC EXERCISE, HAS SHOWN SUPERIOR EFFICACY IN IMPROVING PHYSIOLOGICAL AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES, AND IS ASSOCIATED WITH SUPERIOR ENJOYMENT WHICH MAY INCREASE ADHERENCE TO PA REGIMENS. THE PROPOSED R01 (HEALTH-COG) WILL LEVERAGE THE TWO HEALTH SITES, ADD A NEW UAB SITE, AND ADD NEW MEASURES (PSYCHOLOGICAL MOA MEASURES, COGNITIVE FUNCTION ASSESSMENTS, BIOMARKERS) AND A FEW 12 MONTH FOLLOW-UP TO THE PARENT STUDY. WE ESTIMATE THAT OF OUR PLANNED SAMPLE OF N=100, N=50 WILL BE ENROLLED AT UAB AND N=50 TOTAL AT UW AND UCD. OUR PRIMARY AIM IS TO COMPARE THE EFFECTS OF A 4 MONTH SUPERVISED HIIT OR CME INTERVENTION ON (1) COGNITIVE FUNCTIONING AND (2) SUBJECTIVE COGNITIVE SYMPTOMS. OUR EXPLORATORY AIM IS TO EVALUATE PUTATIVE BIOMARKERS UNDERLYING THE EFFECT OF PA ON COGNITION (BLOOD MARKERS: E.G., BDNF, VEGF, IL-6 AND NEUROIMAGING MARKERS: CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW, RESTING STATE FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY, AND BRAIN VOLUME). OUR SECONDARY AIM IS TO DETERMINE MOA TO LONG-TERM PA MAINTENANCE AT 12 MONTHS. THIS AIM WILL EXAMINE DISTAL PREDICTORS OF LONG-TERM PA, INCLUDING SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC, CLINICAL, AND INTERVENTION FACTORS (I.E., CHANGES IN PARENT R01 PHYSICAL OUTCOMES [CARDIORESPIRATORY FITNESS], CONDITION [HIIT VS CME], [COACHING VS CONTROL]), AS WELL AS PROXIMAL PSYCHOLOGICAL MOA ASSESSED IN REAL-TIME, USING EMA (E.G., SELF-EFFICACY, PERCEIVED BENEFITS, MOTIVATION, SOCIAL SUPPORT). TESTING EFFICACY AND MECHANISMS OF EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS ON COGNITIVE OUTCOMES AND UNDERSTANDING PSYCHOLOGICAL MOA OF HABITUAL PA FOLLOWING SUPERVISED INTERVENTIONS WILL AID IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF PERSONALIZED MEDICINE APPROACHES FOR THE TREATMENT AND PREVENTION OF COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND ADRD IN OLDER PWH.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: IMPROVING CLINICAL TRIAL EFFICIENCY AND QUALITY: RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED EVALUATIONS OF REMOTE VS. IN-PERSON METHODS - REMOTE TRIALS (AKA “VIRTUAL TRIALS” OR “DECENTRALIZED TRIALS”), IN WHICH PATIENTS RECEIVE TREATMENT AND PROVIDE STUDY DATA WITHOUT THE NEED TO TRAVEL TO A CLINIC OR MEDICAL CENTER, HAVE EMERGED AS A PROMISING APPROACH FOR ENHANCING CLINICAL TRIAL EFFICIENCY. HOWEVER, EVIDENCE FOR THE HYPOTHESIZED BENEFITS OF REMOTE TRIALS IS WEAK, CONSISTING PRIMARILY OF ANECDOTAL REPORTS, UNCONTROLLED STUDIES, AND EXPERT OPINION. THE SAME IS TRUE FOR HYPOTHESIZED CHALLENGES AND LIMITATIONS OF REMOTE TRIALS, INCLUDING CONCERNS ABOUT TECHNOLOGICAL BARRIERS AND MULTIPLE ASPECTS OF TRIAL QUALITY. CLEARLY, A STRONGER EVIDENCE BASE IS NEEDED TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF REMOTE TRIALS ON THE “QUALITY AND EFFICIENCY OF TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH, PARTICULARLY MULTISITE TRIALS” (CTSA GOAL 4). RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS (RCTS) ARE THE GOLD STANDARD FOR COMPARING TREATMENTS – AND, BY EXTENSION, FOR TESTING THE IMPACT OF REMOTE METHODS ON TRIAL EFFICIENCY AND QUALITY. ACCORDINGLY, WE PROPOSE AN INNOVATIVE, RIGOROUS EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION OF REMOTE VS. IN-PERSON METHODS ON TRIAL EFFICIENCY (ACCRUAL) AND QUALITY (RETENTION, TREATMENT ADHERENCE, BIO-SPECIMEN COMPLETION RATES), ACROSS 3 RCTS ON 3 DIFFERENT USE CASES: A LARGER, MULTI-SITE DEMONSTRATION TRIAL OF PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR SMOKING CESSATION AT THE BUFFALO AND UPENN HUBS IN THE UG3 PHASE AND TWO SMALLER, SINGLE-SITE DISSEMINATION PROJECTS IN THE UH3 PHASE (A MHEALTH INTERVENTION FOR PEOPLE WITH DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AT THE MUSC HUB; AN OPIOID OVERDOSE EDUCATION AND NALOXONE INTERVENTION AT THE UAB HUB). THESE TRIALS WILL USE A HARMONIZED DESIGN AND OUTCOMES AND FOLLOW PARTICIPANTS THROUGH 3-MONTH FOLLOW-UP. RESULTS FROM THESE 3 RCTS WILL BE ANALYZED JOINTLY TO ASSESS THE DEGREE TO WHICH THE FINDINGS FOR REMOTE VS. IN-PERSON TRIAL METHODS GENERALIZE ACROSS CONDITIONS AND TREATMENT MODALITIES. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE WHETHER USE OF REMOTE VERSUS IN-PERSON METHODS DIFFERENTIALLY IMPACTS REPRESENTATION AND RETENTION ACROSS A RANGE OF PARTICIPANT-LEVEL CHARACTERISTICS (E.G., AGE, PARTICIPANT PREFERENCES). THE PROPOSED SERIES OF RCTS IS SIGNIFICANT AND NOVEL IN ITS ABILITY TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE IMPACT OF REMOTE APPROACHES ON CLINICAL TRIAL EFFICIENCY AND RIGOR. THE QUANTITATIVE, QUALITATIVE, AND COST DATA GENERATED FROM THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE EVIDENCE BASE WHICH WILL GUIDE THE DESIGN OF FUTURE CLINICAL TRIALS. ADDITIONAL DISSEMINATION EFFORTS (E.G., PROJECT WEBSITE, WEBINAR SERIES, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, PUBLICATIONS, NEWSLETTERS AND PRESS RELEASES, AND A NATIONAL WORKSHOP) WILL TARGET THE CTSA CONSORTIUM AND CLINICAL TRIALIST COMMUNITY AT LARGE.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: URBAN AGRICULTURE, WHICH IS DEFINED AS THE GROWING OF FOOD IN AND AROUND CITIES AND ITS INTEGRATION INTO THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ECOLOGICAL FABRIC OF AN URBAN SYSTEM, IS INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS AN IMPORTANT COMPONENT OF A SUSTAINABLE FOOD SYSTEM. WHETHER THROUGH COMMUNITY FARMS OR, WITH THE ADVENT OF HYDROPONIC TECHNOLOGY, INDOOR COMMERCIAL FARMING SPACE, URBAN AGRICULTURE PRESENTS THE OPPORTUNITY TO GROW LOCAL, EASILY-TRANSPORTABLE FRESH PRODUCE THAT FACILITATES ACCESS TO HEALTHY FOOD, IMPROVES FOOD SECURITY, AND CREATES SKILLED JOBS FOR LOCAL RESIDENTS.BUILDING A WORKFORCE SKILLED IN THE NUANCES OF URBAN AGRICULTURE - BOTH SOIL-BASED AND HYDROPONIC - IS CRUCIAL TO GROWING THIS SECTOR. NEW YORK CITY IS A PRIME LOCATION FOR EXPANDING THE FIELD: THE CITY ALREADY HAS A STRONG NETWORK, PRACTICE, AND CULTURE OF URBAN FARMING, FROM THE MORE THAN 700 COMMUNITY GARDENS THROUGHOUT FIVE BOROUGHS, MANY OF WHICH BEGAN ON ABANDONED BUILDING LOTS AND NOW ARE PROTECTED, TO A RAPIDLY-GROWING COMMERCIAL FARMING INDUSTRY. IT ALSO HAS ROBUST COMMUNITY-BASED MOVEMENTS AND LOCAL POLICY INITIATIVES CENTERED AROUND FOOD SECURITY, LOCAL FOOD ACCESS, AND THEIR INTERSECTION WITH ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE. NEEDED, HOWEVER, ARE OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOUTH AND YOUNG ADULTS TO FORMALLY TRAIN AND BUILD THE SKILLS THEY NEED TO PARTICIPATE EQUITABLY IN THIS GROWING SECTOR.NY SUN WORKS, A NON-PROFIT LEADER IN K-12 SUSTAINABLE URBAN AGRICULTURE EDUCATION IN NYC, IS WELL-POSITIONED TO ADDRESS THIS NEED. WE BUILD HYDROPONIC CLASSROOMS IN CITY SCHOOLS, PAIRING THEM WITH OUR GRADE-SPECIFIC CURRICULUM AND COMPREHENSIVE TEACHER TRAINING, TO TEACH SCIENCE, SUSTAINABILITY, AND CLIMATE EDUCATION THROUGH HYDROPONIC FARMING. STUDENTS MASTER SEED-TO-HARVEST HYDROPONIC FARMING AND GROW HUNDREDS OF POUNDS OF FRESH PRODUCE TO SHARE WITH THEIR FAMILIES WHILE ALSO DIVING INTO CORE SCIENCE CONTENT, SUSTAINABILITY AND CLIMATE EDUCATION. WE CURRENTLY SERVE OVER 300 SCHOOLS THROUGHOUT THE CITY, REACHING 120,000 STUDENTS IN THE 2023-24 SCHOOL YEAR, WITH A FOCUS ON SUPPORTING STUDENTS IN HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES. IN 2022, WE ALSO LAUNCHED THE CITY'S FIRST CONTROLLED ENVIRONMENT AGRICULTURE (CEA) WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, WHICH WAS DEVELOPED WITH FUNDING FROM USDA-UAIP AND FOLLOWS CORNELL UNIVERSITY'S INDOOR FARMING PROGRAM FRAMEWORK. THE PROGRAM EQUIPS HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WITH TECHNICAL SKILLS, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE KNOWLEDGE, AND WORKFORCE READINESS TRAINING WHILE BUILDING PATHWAYS FOR HIGH SCHOOL GRADUATES TO PARTICIPATE EQUITABLY ON NEW YORK'S GREEN ECONOMY.WITH THE SPECA GRANT, NY SUN WORKS WILL BE ABLE TO: 1) UPGRADE OUR CURRENT URBAN AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT CURRICULUM TO MEET COMMUNITY COLLEGE-LEVEL COURSE STANDARDS; 2) SECURE CPL (CREDIT FOR PRIOR LEARNING) APPROVAL AT THE ASSOCIATE'S DEGREE LEVEL FROM LAGUARDIA COMMUNITY COLLEGE, A TWO-YEAR COLLEGE WITHIN THE CITY UNIVERSITY OF NY SYSTEM; 3) TRAIN 12 CEA SCIENCE TEACHERS IN THE RE,VISED CURRICULUM; 4) REACH AN ESTIMATED 650+ STUDENTS OVER THE COURSE OF THE GRANT CYCLE WITH EXPANDED CEA TRAINING; AND 5) ASSESS STUDENT OUTCOMES, INCLUDING STUDENT POST-SECONDARY MATRICULATION RATES, TO EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF THE CPL OPPORTUNITY ON STUDENT DECISIONS TO PURSUE POST-SECONDARY OPPORTUNITIES AT LAGUARDIA.THESE INITIATIVES WILL SUPPORT SEVERAL KEY AGRICULTURE POLICY PRIORITIES BY ENHANCING URBAN AGRICULTURE EDUCATION CURRICULA; DECREASING BARRIERS TO AND ENCOURAGING INTEREST IN POST-SECONDARY STUDY IN THE SUSTAINABLE URBAN AGRICULTURE FIELD, PARTICULARLY FOR STUDENTS FROM LOW-INCOME HISTORICALLY UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS; AND, BY FACILITATING OPPORTUNITIES FOR POST-SECONDARY STUDY, GROWING THE PIPELINE OF SKILLED WORKERS ENTERING THE FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SECTORS. THESE INITIATIVES FURTHER ADDRESS THE OVERARCHING NEED TO SUPPORT EQUITABLE ACCESS TO HIGHER EDUCATION FOR STUDENTS FROM HISTORICALLY UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES. INTRODUCING STUDENTS TO POSTSECONDARY PROGRAMS AND PROVIDING CREDIT FOR PRIOR LEARNING WILL DECREASE BARRIERS TO ENTRY AND SUPPORT ONGOING STUDENT SUCCESS (FOR EXAMPLE, STUDIES SHOW THAT CREDIT FOR PRIOR LEARNING INCREASES STUDENT PERSISTENCE AND IMPROVES STUDENT OUTCOMES IN POSTSECONDARY PROGRAMS). IN ADDITION, THE TRAINING WE WILL PROVIDE TO HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS IN CURRICULUM IMPLEMENTATION AND HYDROPONIC FARMING SKILLS WILL BUILD TEACHERS' SKILLS AND EXPAND THE PROGRAM'S REACH TO SUCCESSIVE COHORTS OF STUDENTS EVEN AFTER THE GRANT CYCLE CONCLUDES, SUPPORTING URBAN AGRICULTURE EDUCATION OVER THE LONG-TERM. ?

prime_award_base_transaction_description: ASSESSING COGNITIVE FUNCTIONING IN THE NATIONAL MONITORING THE FUTURE (MTF) PANEL STUDY - ABSTRACT EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES AND SUBSTANCE USE ARE KEY EXPOSURES FOR COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD) THAT ARISE IN ADOLESCENCE AND YOUNG ADULTHOOD. EDUCATION IS THE STRONGEST KNOWN PROTECTIVE FACTOR FOR COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND AD/ADRD RISK. SUBSTANCE USE IS A MAIN RISK FACTOR FOR ACUTE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT, ALTHOUGH THERE IS LESS EVIDENCE REGARDING ITS ROLE IN AD/ADRD DEVELOPMENT. A COMBINATION OF DETAILED DATA ON LIFE COURSE SUBSTANCE USE AND COGNITIVE DATA IS NEEDED. THE MONITORING THE FUTURE (MTF) PANEL STUDY OFFERS AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO EXAMINE HOW EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES AND SUBSTANCE USE FROM ADOLESCENCE THROUGH ADULTHOOD ARE ASSOCIATED WITH MIDLIFE COGNITIVE FUNCTION. THE MTF PANEL STUDY HAS BEEN CONTINUOUSLY FUNDED BY NIH SINCE 1975 AND FOLLOWS A NEW NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE OF 2,450 12TH GRADE STUDENTS EACH YEAR. THE PANEL CURRENTLY INCLUDES 50 COHORTS FROM EVERY HIGH SCHOOL CLASS FROM 1976 TO 2025 (TOTAL N~120,000). RESPONDENTS ARE FIRST SURVEYED AS STUDENTS IN HIGH SCHOOL AT MODAL AGE 18 AND FOLLOWED REGULARLY THROUGHOUT THE LIFE COURSE; THE OLDEST COHORTS HAVE BEEN SURVEYED AT AGE 65. THE CURRENT PROPOSAL AIMS TO EXAMINE EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES AND SUBSTANCE USE FROM ADOLESCENCE THROUGH ADULTHOOD AS RISK FACTORS FOR AD/ADRD BY ADDING MEASURES OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION TO THE MTF PANEL. THE PROPOSED COGNITIVE MEASURES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED AND USED BY THE HEALTH AND RETIREMENT STUDY (HRS) AND THE UNDERSTANDING AMERICA STUDY (UAS) FOR ONLINE ADMINISTRATION. WEB- BASED MEASURES ASSESSING MEMORY, NUMERACY, EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONING, WORD KNOWLEDGE, AND FLUID INTELLIGENCE, WILL BE ADDED TO THE MTF PANEL AS A HEALTHY BRAINS MODULE FOR N~9,600 ELIGIBLE MTF PANEL PARTICIPANTS WHO WILL BE AGES 50, 55, 60, OR 65 IN 2026 AND 2027. THESE PARTICIPANTS WERE ENROLLED IN THE MTF PANEL STUDY AT AGE 18 WHILE IN HIGH SCHOOL FROM 1979/1980 FOR THOSE AGE 65 THROUGH 1994/1995 FOR THOSE AGE 50, ROUGHLY CORRESPONDING TO BIRTH COHORTS 1961-1977. WE CONSERVATIVELY ESTIMATE OBTAINING COGNITIVE TESTING DATA FROM N~5,800 PARTICIPANTS. WE WILL ALSO CAPTURE A BROAD RANGE OF SELF-REPORTED HEALTH BEHAVIORS AND PARADATA ON RESPONSE TIME AND KEYSTROKE ERRORS. THE STUDY'S SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO EXAMINE: (1) ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCES (SELF-REPORTED) AND EDUCATION QUALITY (FROM NATIONAL CENTER FOR EDUCATIONAL STATISTICS [NCES] ADMINISTRATIVE DATA) IN RELATION TO MIDLIFE COGNITION ASSESSED BY THE PROPOSED HEALTHY BRAINS MODULE AT AGES 50 TO 65, (2) SUBSTANCE USE ACROSS THE LIFESPAN IN RELATION TO MIDLIFE COGNITION, AND (3) SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC MODERATORS OF THE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN EDUCATION AND SUBSTANCE USE WITH MIDLIFE COGNITION. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL PROVIDE AN EXCEPTIONAL DATA RESOURCE TO EXAMINE RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS FROM ADOLESCENCE THROUGH ADULTHOOD AND SUBSEQUENT MIDLIFE COGNITIVE FUNCTIONING IN A LARGE, NATIONAL SAMPLE WITH LONGITUDINAL DATA ACROSS THE LIFE COURSE.

funding_opportunity_goals_text:
THE GOALS ARE:

  • TO FOSTER FUNDAMENTAL CREATIVE DISCOVERIES, INNOVATIVE RESEARCH STRATEGIES, AND THEIR APPLICATIONS AS A BASIS FOR ULTIMATELY PROTECTING AND IMPROVING HEALTH;
  • TO DEVELOP, MAINTAIN, AND RENEW SCIENTIFIC HUMAN AND PHYSICAL RESOURCES THAT WILL ENSURE THE NATION'S CAPABILITY TO PREVENT DISEASE;
  • TO EXPAND THE KNOWLEDGE BASE IN MEDICAL AND ASSOCIATED SCIENCES IN ORDER TO ENHANCE THE NATION'S ECONOMIC WELL-BEING AND ENSURE A CONTINUED HIGH RETURN ON THE PUBLIC INVESTMENT IN RESEARCH; AND
  • TO EXEMPLIFY AND PROMOTE THE HIGHEST LEVEL OF SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY, PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY, AND SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY IN THE CONDUCT OF SCIENCE.

IN REALIZING THESE GOALS, THE NIH PROVIDES LEADERSHIP AND DIRECTION TO PROGRAMS DESIGNED TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF THE NATION BY CONDUCTING AND SUPPORTING RESEARCH:

  • IN THE CAUSES, DIAGNOSIS, PREVENTION, AND CURE OF HUMAN DISEASES;
  • IN THE PROCESSES OF HUMAN GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT;
  • IN THE BIOLOGICAL EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS;
  • IN THE UNDERSTANDING OF MENTAL, ADDICTIVE AND PHYSICAL DISORDERS; AND
  • IN DIRECTING PROGRAMS FOR THE COLLECTION, DISSEMINATION, AND EXCHANGE OF INFORMATION IN MEDICINE AND HEALTH, INCLUDING THE DEVELOPMENT AND SUPPORT OF MEDICAL LIBRARIES AND THE TRAINING OF MEDICAL LIBRARIANS AND OTHER HEALTH INFORMATION SPECIALISTS.
prime_award_base_transaction_description: LUNG-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS OF TB PROGRESSION - TUBERCULOSIS (TB) REMAINS AMONG THE LEADING CAUSES OF DEATH WORLDWIDE, AND CURRENT THERAPIES AND VACCINES HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO FULLY CONTROL THE DISEASE. INCREASING TRANSMISSION OF ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT FORMS OF MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS (MTB) REQUIRES A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF DISEASE MECHANISMS TO DEVELOP MORE EFFICIENT PREVENTION AND THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES.  A KEY ASPECT OF MTB’S EVOLUTIONARY SUCCESS IS ITS ABILITY TO EXPLOIT THE PULMONARY ENVIRONMENT AND CAUSE LUNG DAMAGE TO ENSURE TRANSMISSION AMONG HUMANS BY AEROSOL. PERSISTENT LUNG DAMAGE IS ALSO A MAJOR CAUSE OF TB- ASSOCIATED MORTALITY AND POST-TUBERCULOSIS MORBIDITY AFTER MICROBIOLOGICAL CURE. THE PULMONARY TB (PTB) TYPICALLY OCCURS IN IMMUNOCOMPETENT, BUT TB SUSCEPTIBLE INDIVIDUALS, OFTEN DESPITE VACCINATION AND PREEXISTING IMMUNITY, BUT THE LUNG-SPECIFIC FACTORS ALLOWING FOR PTB PROGRESSION REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD.  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSAL IS TO EXPLORE LUNG-SPECIFIC FACTORS THAT SUPPORT MTB SURVIVAL AND PROPAGATION IN THE LUNGS OF IMMUNOCOMPETENT HOSTS. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DYSPLASTIC EPITHELIAL CELLS WITHIN PTB LESIONS REPRESENT A DYSREGULATED REGENERATION OF THE AIRWAY AND ALVEOLAR PROGENITORS, AND THEIR CROSSTALK WITH IMMUNE AND MESENCHYMAL CELLS PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN ORCHESTRATING THE FORMATION OF THE PERMISSIVE PULMONARY NICHE FOR MTB AND DRIVES THE PTB PROGRESSION TOWARDS FIBRO-NECROTIC LESIONS.  USING MOUSE MODELS THAT DISPLAY NECROTIC LUNG LESIONS, RESEMBLING THOSE SEEN IN HUMAN PTB AND ANALYZING HUMAN TB LESIONS, THE STUDY WILL FOCUS ON THE INTERACTION BETWEEN DYSPLASTIC EPITHELIAL CELLS AND MACROPHAGES, AND HOW THESE CELLS CREATE A NICHE FOR MTB IMMUNE EVASION. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST THAT THAT DYSPLASTIC EPITHELIAL CELLS WITHIN PTB LESIONS INDUCE AND RECRUIT “REPAIR” MACROPHAGES THAT, IN THE CONTEXT OF CHRONIC PTB LESIONS, COMPROMISE LOCAL IMMUNITY. THE ORIGINS AND ROLES OF THESE DYSPLASTIC CELLS REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN.  THE RESEARCH IS ORGANIZED AROUND THREE AIMS. THE FIRST AIM IS TO TRACE THE DEVELOPMENTAL ORIGINS OF THE DYSPLASTIC EPITHELIAL CELLS USING LINEAGE-TRACING TECHNIQUES AND TEST WHETHER EGFR INHIBITORS CAN LIMIT THEIR EXPANSION. THE SECOND AIM FOCUSES ON  REPAIR  MACROPHAGES, CHARACTERIZED BY ARG1 EXPRESSION, AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH DYSPLASTIC EPITHELIAL CELLS, WHICH MAY PROMOTE AN IMMUNOSUPPRESSIVE ENVIRONMENT THAT SUPPORTS MTB GROWTH. WE WILL TEST WHETHER CSF1 PRODUCED BY REACTIVE LUNG EPITHELIUM PROMOTES PTB PROGRESSION USING CSF1R INHIBITORS. THE THIRD AIM INVOLVES A COLLABORATION WITH UAB TO COMPARE HUMAN AND MOUSE PTB LESIONS USING ADVANCED TECHNIQUES LIKE MULTIPLEXED IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS AND REVEAL COMMON PATHWAYS OF EPITHELIAL- MACROPHAGE CROSSTALK.  BY EXPLORING LUNG-SPECIFIC TB MECHANISMS, THIS PROJECT COULD GUIDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL HOST-DIRECTED THERAPIES TO DECREASE LUNG DAMAGE AND REDUCE MTB TRANSMISSION. THIS RESEARCH WILL ALSO CONTRIBUTE TO A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLES OF ABORTIVE REGENERATION AND EPITHELIAL DYSPLASIA IN OTHER LUNG DISEASES.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: CHEROKEE NARCH, NATIVE AMERICAN RESEARCH CENTERS FOR HEALTH (NARCH) - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SIGNIFICANT HEALTH CHALLENGES CONTINUE TO IMPACT TRIBAL NATIONS, YET THERE REMAINS A SEVERE SHORTAGE OF SCIENTISTS CONDUCTING TRIBALLY ENGAGED RESEARCH AIMED AT ALLEVIATING HEALTH DISPARITIES AFFECTING MEMBERS OF TRIBAL NATIONS. FOR SEVERAL YEARS, CHEROKEE NATION (CN), THE UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA HEALTH SCIENCES CENTER (OUHS), AND THE OKLAHOMA STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF OSTEOPATHIC MEDICINE (OSU-COM) AT CN HAVE PARTNERED TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE BY BUILDING TRIBAL RESEARCH CAPACITY THROUGH THE NATIVE AMERICAN RESEARCH CENTERS FOR HEALTH (NARCH) MECHANISM. IN THE CURRENT FUNDING CYCLE, THE PARTNERSHIP AMONG CN, OUHS, AND OSU-COM CONTINUES TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND CAREER ENHANCEMENT ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONALLY, THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS FOR MEDICAL SCIENCES (UAMS) HAS JOINED CHEROKEE NARCH AS A NEW RESEARCH PARTNER. THE OVERALL MISSION OF CHEROKEE NARCH IS TO DEVELOP A DURABLE RESEARCH CAPACITY AND CAREER ENHANCEMENT PATHWAYS WITHIN THE LARGEST TRIBAL NATION BY POPULATION IN THE UNITED STATES, THEREBY IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF THE TRIBAL POPULATION IN NORTHEASTERN OKLAHOMA. TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL, THE FIVE SPECIFIC AIMS OF CHEROKEE NARCH ARE: 1) TO STRENGTHEN ADMINISTRATIVE INFRASTRUCTURE, INCLUDING A LEADERSHIP TEAM (LT) AND A TRIBAL-CAMPUS ADVISORY COMMITTEE (TCAC), ENSURING THE INTEGRATION OF CAREER ENHANCEMENT, RESEARCH INFRASTRUCTURE, AND RESEARCH ACTIVITIES; 2) TO EDUCATE THE NEXT GENERATION OF RESEARCHERS WHO CAN ENGAGE IN TRIBALLY RELEVANT RESEARCH IN PARTNERSHIP WITH CN, FOCUSING ON UNDERGRADUATE, AND HEALTH PROFESSIONS STUDENTS; 3) TO BUILD TRIBAL RESEARCH CAPACITY BY DEVELOPING INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) RESEARCH, A GROWING CONCERN AMONG TRIBAL CITIZENS RECEIVING CARE AT CNHS; 4) TO CONDUCT INNOVATIVE RESEARCH THAT SEEDS FUTURE PROJECTS LED BY INVESTIGATORS WORKING WITHIN THE CHEROKEE NATION CONTEXT; AND; 5) TO EVALUATE ALL PARTNERSHIP ACTIVITIES, INCLUDING MONITORING STUDENT CAREER PROGRESSION, INFRASTRUCTURE AND CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS, RESEARCH PROJECT OUTCOMES, AND THE OVERALL EFFECTIVENESS OF THE CHEROKEE NATION NARCH PROGRAM. CHEROKEE NARCH PROVIDES A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO SOLIDIFY THE FOUNDATION FOR TRIBAL CAPACITY IN HEALTH RESEARCH. THE COMBINED STRENGTHS OF OUHS AND OSU-COM AT CN IN CAREER ENHANCEMENT SIGNIFICANTLY STRENGTHEN THIS APPLICATION, AS BOTH INSTITUTIONS HAVE DEMONSTRATED SUCCESS IN COLLABORATING WITH CN AND IN TRAINING STUDENTS INTERESTED IN TRIBAL RESEARCH AND HEALTHCARE, INCLUDING THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE FIRST TRIBALLY AFFILIATED MEDICAL SCHOOL IN THE UNITED STATES AT OSU-COM AT CN. THE ADDITION OF UAMS AS A RESEARCH PARTNER FURTHER EXPANDS THE SCOPE AND EXPERTISE OF THE COLLABORATION. CHEROKEE NARCH THUS OFFERS AN UNPRECEDENTED ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH A TRIBAL NATION AND THREE RESEARCH-INTENSIVE UNIVERSITIES, TWO OF WHICH, OUHS AND OSU-COM AT CN, SERVE LARGE NUMBERS OF TRIBALLY ENROLLED STUDENTS, WILL WORK SYNERGISTICALLY TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF THE TRIBAL POPULATION SERVED BY CHEROKEE NATION.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: ACQUISITION OF MOLECULAR CHARACTERIZATION INSTRUMENTATION TO ADVANCE MASS SPECTROMETRY CAPABILITIES FOR RESEARCH AND TEACHING AT AMERICA'S ARCTIC UNIVERSITY - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ACQUIRE A THERMO SCIENTIFIC TSQ QUANTIS PLUS TRIPLE QUADRUPOLE MASS SPECTROMETER (MS) COUPLED WITH A VANQUISH FLEX ULTRA-HIGH-PRESSURE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPH (UHPLC), CAPABLE OF TANDEM MASS SPECTROMETRY (MS/MS). THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF), WHICH OFFERS THE ONLY AMERICAN CHEMICAL SOCIETY (ACS) ACCREDITED CHEMISTRY DEGREE IN ALASKA, CURRENTLY LACKS AN UHPLC-MS/MS TO TRAIN STUDENTS IN MODERN ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES TO MEET WORKFORCE DEMANDS OR SUPPORT CUTTING EDGE ARCTIC RESEARCH. THE PROPOSED UHPLC-MS/MS WILL ENHANCE BIOMEDICAL AND CRITICAL ARCTIC BASED RESEARCH AND SUPPORT LOCAL TEACHING CAPACITY. UAF IS THE LEADING RESEARCH UNIVERSITY IN ALASKA, THE NATION’S PREMIER ARCTIC UNIVERSITY, AND MAINTAINS UNPARALLELED ACCESS TO THE ARCTIC, ITS RESOURCES AND UNIQUE NORTHERN BIOMEDICAL MODELS. IN THE BIOMEDICAL FIELD, UAF IS AN INTERNATIONAL LEADER IN HIBERNATION RESEARCH AND HOUSES THE CENTER FOR TRANSFORMATIVE RESEARCH IN METABOLISM (TRIM), THE FIRST NIH SUPPORTED CENTER IN THE U.S. UTILIZING MAMMALIAN HIBERNATION AS A BIOMEDICAL MODEL OF NATURAL TOLERANCE TO METABOLIC EXTREMES, HEALTHY OBESITY, AVOIDANCE OF BONE AND MUSCLE ATROPHY DUE TO DISUSE, AND RESISTANCE TO ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY. IN ARCTIC- BASED RESEARCH, UAF OPERATES ONE OF THE LARGEST ARCTIC RESEARCH STATIONS IN THE US AND ONE OF THE MOST SOPHISTICATED UNIVERSITY RESEARCH VESSELS IN THE WORLD. GIVEN OUR UNIQUE LOCATION, UAF RESEARCHERS STUDY NORTHERN, PLACE-BASED ARCTIC AND BIOMEDICAL QUESTIONS WHICH CANNOT BE ADDRESSED AT LOCATIONS ANYWHERE ELSE IN THE US AND ACQUISITION OF A UHPLC-MS/MS WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT THIS BROAD RANGE OF RESEARCH.  THIS INSTRUMENT WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT TRAINING OF STUDENTS IN MODERN ANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES AND BE INCORPORATED INTO 6 CLASSROOM TRAINING, SUPPORTING RESEARCH-BASED EDUCATION, THAT WILL HELP INCREASE THE TALENT POOL ON WHICH THE U.S. BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH ENTERPRISE AND ALASKAN INDUSTRY CAN DRAW. ACQUISITION OF THIS INSTRUMENT WILL LARGELY ADVANCE THE CAPACITY TO PERFORM MOLECULAR STRUCTURE AND FLUX ANALYSIS AND SUPPORT ACQUISITION OF DATA TO SUPPORT NIH GRANT PROPOSALS FOR 11 FACULTY MEMBERS AT UAF (INCLUDING 5 MAJOR USERS AND 6 MINOR USERS), 6 OF WHOM ARE EARLY CAREER FACULTY IN DEPARTMENT OF BIOLOGY AND WILDLIFE, DEPARTMENT OF VETERINARY MEDICINE, DEPARTMENT OF CHEMISTRY AND BIOCHEMISTRY, INSTITUTE OF ARCTIC BIOLOGY, AND THE COLLEGE OF FISHERIES AND OCEAN SCIENCES. ALL FACULTY INVOLVED WITH THIS INSTRUMENT HAVE A HISTORY OF ENGAGING GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN RESEARCH. WE HAVE TECHNICAL SUPPORT TO MAINTAIN THE INSTRUMENTS WITHOUT ADDING ADDITIONAL WORKLOAD ON ASSISTANT PROFESSORS AND WE HAVE SUFFICIENT FUNDING TO SUPPORT USE OF THE INSTRUMENTS.
